variplex: analysis of strong dependency and conflict graphs of variability models

Source: R/variplex-package.R
variplex-package.Rd

variplex computes, for a variability model, every relationship between two features that holds in all its valid configurations, and analyses the resulting graphs.

Details

  • vp_generate() reads a feature model in UVL, or the Boolean formula (DIMACS) of a model written in any other notation, such as the Kconfig files of Linux, and computes the requires, excludes and at-least-one graphs with a SAT solver.

  • More than a hundred functions, all named vp_*, answer questions about the graphs and return tibbles: measures of each feature, the hierarchy, conflicts and their causes, configuration, teams, combinatorial testing, network patterns and the evolution of a model through its versions. vp_functions() lists them by topic.

  • vp_plot() draws a model or part of it; vp_dot() gives the Graphviz source of the drawing.

Start with vignette("variplex"). The graphs hold relationships between two features only: a rule that ties three or more features at once is in no graph, unless it implies a relationship between two of them (vignette("limits-theory", package = "variplex")).

The engine is Strong4VM (https://github.com/rheradio/strong4vm), whose C++ code, with the SAT solver Glucose 3.0, the backbone solver BoneDigger and the ANTLR 4 parser runtime, is compiled into the package.
